title: Pilot Sprint 3 - Go‑Live Dress Rehearsal & Traffic Gating
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on final dress rehearsal for pilot cutover. Reviewed recent perf numbers, confirmed canary thresholds and A/B routing matrix, discussed monitoring hooks and runbook responsibilities. Agreed on dry-run date and deliverables for security and SLO gating.
topics: Review of last week's latency/cost telemetry
Canary gating thresholds and roll percentage schedule
A/B routing with fallback to hosted variants
Monitoring/alerting hooks and smoke test steps
Runbook owner assignments and dry-run schedule
Security checklist: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts
transcript:
Header: 2026-04-14 15:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Eli (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM); Samir (Velox), Olivia (ML), James (SRE), Hannah (Security)
---
00:00 Maya: okay hey everyone thanks for joining we are on for the sprint three dress rehearsal, quick agenda pass, we want to walk the canary plan, smoke tests, and final owners.
00:18 Samir: yep thanks maya, quick context we hit the perf targets last week but saw a couple of latency spikes when sequence lengths exceeded 1.2k tokens. olivia dug in a bit.
00:28 Olivia: yeah the tail latency spiked at about 540ms for P95 and P99 went up to 1.1s, we think it was a KV cache miss pattern from some long chat sessions. not sure if it's caching config or the client prefixing.
00:45 Eli: mhm we saw that in the batch logs, there were a lot of new conversation ids that invalidated prefix cache, so the runtime didn't reuse KV cache effectively. we suggested enabling prefix-based caching with a 30m TTL and bumping batching threshold to 64 for those endpoints.
01:05 James: would that increase cost? we are sensitive to token cost in prod.
01:12 Priya: tradeoff yes, a little more memory but lower tail latency — cost profile shows lower per-token cost when batching and cache hits are high. we can share the spreadsheet.
01:25 Maya: action item we'll attach the batch/caching cost model.
01:30 Hannah: on security side, quick question about KMS: will customer-managed keys be available for private deployment or only hosted?
01:38 Eli: for Private we support customer KMS/HSM, for hosted we offer optional CMK integration with audit logs exported to your SIEM. the logs include token level metadata but not raw inputs. there might be naming differences in the export.
01:55 Hannah: okay please send the SOC2 artifact and the log schema.
02:00 Maya: noted — we'll add to the repo link.
02:08 Samir: let's go through the canary plan, how are we gating? what's the abort criteria?
02:15 Eli: proposed gating: run smoke test suite, then 1% traffic for 30 minutes, monitor 5 metrics: request success rate, P95 latency, P99 latency, error types (OOM, rate), and semantic quality via synthetic prompts. abort if success rate <99% or P99 > 1.5s or semantic regressions flagged on our eval set.
02:43 Olivia: semantic checks — can you clarify how auto-eval flags regressions? we've had false positives before.
02:50 Eli: good point. we run a curated prompt set (200 items) and use top-k NLI scoring for label drift. if aggregate quality drops by >3% we flag; but for noise we require sustained drop across two consecutive runs. it's noisy so we recommend human spot-check at the 1% step.
03:12 James: for A/B experiments we want to route 10% to experimental model and 90% to baseline with feature flagging. if errors spike, traffic should fallback to baseline automatically. how quick is the fallback?
03:25 Eli: fallback is immediate for infrastructure errors (timeouts/500s). for quality gates we have a decision window of 30 minutes with manual override. we can shorten to 10 if you want more aggressive detection.
03:36 Samir: let's keep it at 30 to give the model time to stabilize.
03:42 Maya: okay noted. next, runbook roles — who is primary for rollback?
03:47 James: SRE on call will own rollback and blue‑green shift. Olivia will own model behavior checks, Hannah runs security verification for logged events.
03:57 Maya: we'll document those owners in the runbook.
04:05 Priya: dry run scheduling — proposed friday 2026-04-17 02:00 UTC (quiet window) for a full rehearsal including traffic shift and rollback.
04:13 Samir: that time is okay for us.
04:16 Olivia: question about telemetry endpoints — we need a dedicated metrics namespace in your console to pull P95/P99 and token cost by route.
04:24 Eli: yes we can provision a per-route dashboard and grant read-only tokens to your grafana via API. we'll also push the events to your telemetry sink.
04:36 Hannah: must ensure audit logs are retained for 90 days at minimum for PCI audits.
04:41 Eli: retention can be configured; we'll confirm retention policy for your plan.
04:47 Maya: sharing link to the draft runbook: https://redwood.app/runbooks/velox-sprint3-dressrehearsal (doc link)
04:55 Samir: thanks, we'll review.
05:00 Olivia: small nit — quantization fallback. if GPU memory becomes constrained do you have an automatic switch to a quantized variant?
05:09 Eli: we do support automatic fallback to an int8 quantized model in Dedicated and Private. hosted can also route to a lighter variant but there is a latency delta. config key is modelVariantPreference in the routing policy.
05:24 Maya: let's talk about cost gates — if cost per 1k tokens increases by more than 20% vs baseline we should pause rollout. agree?
05:33 James: yes that's fine. can we get a rolling 1h metric?
05:36 Eli: we'll add a rolling 1h cost rate to the dashboard and an alert.
05:40 Maya: ok moving on to canned smoke tests — list is below, we'll run them during the dry run: 1) health check endpoint, 2) latency spike test with variable sequence lengths, 3) KV cache-miss regen test, 4) A/B quality spot-checks, 5) end-to-end downstream integration call.
06:04 Olivia: for the KV cache-miss test, can we simulate new conversation ids at a rate to mimic worst-case?
06:12 Eli: yes we have a harness script we'll hand over. link in notes.
06:17 Priya: I'll share the harness and the script with expected pass/fail thresholds.
06:21 Maya: Security — Hannah anything else?
06:24 Hannah: two things: we need SSO with SCIM provisioning before production cutover and confirmation that tokens are rotated monthly. also need to confirm there is no plaintext persistence of PII in logs.
06:36 Eli: SSO/SCIM is supported; token rotation is configurable, and logs are redacted by default for payloads. we'll provide the config and policy docs.
06:45 Samir: what's the expected time to rollback to baseline if we trigger a circuit breaker?
06:49 James: technically a traffic switch is immediate but the effective recovery of downstream caches may take a few minutes. we should expect a 5–10 minute stabilization window.
06:58 Maya: noted. we will capture that in the runbook timeline.
07:05 Olivia: can we talk about canary duration? you suggested 30 minutes at 1% then step up to 5% for an hour, then 20% for 2 hours. is that typical?
07:15 Eli: yes that's our recommended ramp. alternative is a fast path: 1% for 15m, 10% for 30m, then 50% if metrics look good. we can do either.
07:29 Samir: prefer the slower ramp — our downstream is chat-heavy and we want time to observe semantic regressions.
07:35 Maya: slower ramp selected.
07:38 Priya: mapping owners for each checkpoint: 1% — Olivia to validate quality and James for infra; 5% — Maya/Eli pair to monitor costs; 20% — Samir to sign off for product readiness.
07:52 Samir: agree but final sign-off remains Samir as platform lead.
07:56 Maya: good. now tickets: latency debugging — olivia had a follow-up with some logs?
07:59 Olivia: yes I posted a sample trace in the ticket, it shows per-token kernel stalls when sequence length jumps. looks like a kernel selection mismatch.
08:10 Eli: we'll run a microbenchmark and may flip kernel selection to the pack-fused path for long sequences; we'll share results by tuesday.
08:19 Maya: next, compliance docs — Hannah wants SOC2 and export schema by EOD Monday?
08:25 Hannah: by EOD Tuesday is better. monday is tight.
08:29 Maya: ok EOD Tuesday.
08:32 Priya: dry-run checklist recap: instances provisioned, dashboards created, harness scripts shared, runbook owners documented, security docs provided, smoke test thresholds in doc.
08:42 James: can we add a step to pre-warm KV caches with historical prefixes to reduce cold-start misses during canary?
08:49 Eli: yes we can push a pre-warm job before the 1% step. that's part of the harness.
08:55 Maya: great. any blockers?
08:58 Samir: only one — we need a final cost commitment for pilot week to avoid surprises. can you provide an estimated spend cap?
09:06 Maya: we can give a capped estimate and set an alert at 80% of that cap, but actual billing is usage-based. we'll provide a cap recommendation.
09:15 Olivia: question about routing by geography — if we need to route EU traffic to EU-only model variant can that be done?
09:22 Eli: yes routing policy supports geo-based routing and region fallbacks. data residency options exist in Private deployment.
09:30 Maya: excellent. last part: dry run smoke schedule and responsibilities. I'll read it: Friday 02:00 UTC — 00:00-00:10 health check, 00:10-00:30 1% canary + smoke tests, 00:30-01:30 5% stabilization + quality eval, 01:30-03:30 20% soak, 03:30-04:00 rollback rehearsal and postmortem. owners as earlier.
09:58 Samir: sounds good.
10:02 Hannah: confirm we get the audit log schema after the call.
10:06 Maya: yes EOD Tuesday.
10:09 Priya: i'll follow up with calendar invite for dry run and include runbook link.
10:13 Olivia: thanks all.
10:15 Maya: any final Qs?
10:17 James: none.
10:18 Maya: ok we'll send the runbook update, cost model, harness scripts and schedule. thanks everyone.
10:25 Meeting end.
